updates.name: Edmund Brodie
updates.bio: Evolutionary biologist who holds the B.F.D. Runk Professorship in Botany in the University of Virginia's Department of Biology and directs Mountain Lake Biological Station. His work asks how selection and genetic mechanisms jointly drive evolution, emphasizing coevolutionary arms races between reptile and amphibian predators and their prey, plus social selection and indirect genetic effects studied in insects.
updates.research_interests: predator-prey coevolutionary arms races in reptiles and amphibians; antipredator adaptation; phenotypic and genetic integration; quantitative genetics of natural selection; indirect genetic effects and social selection in insects

updates.name: Edward A.G. Schuur
updates.bio: Ecosystem ecologist at Northern Arizona University's Center for Ecosystem Science and Society and Department of Biological Sciences. He studies how Arctic ecosystems feed back to a warming climate, especially how much permafrost soil carbon thaws and escapes as CO2 and methane, how fast, and in what form, with summer field research in Alaska.
updates.research_interests: permafrost carbon release as CO2 and methane; Arctic ecosystem responses to climate warming; terrestrial ecosystem-climate feedbacks; plant-soil-atmosphere carbon exchange; disturbance effects on ecosystems; radiocarbon dating
updates.current_affiliation: Northern Arizona University, Center for Ecosystem Science and Society
updates.notes: Evidence: 'Ted Schuur, Ph.D. ... Professor of Ecosystem Ecology Center for Ecosystem Sciences and Society'. His project links include the US-EML AmeriFlux site, the BNZ LTER and the Permafrost Carbon Network.

updates.name: Edward P. Dever
updates.bio: Physical oceanographer and professor in Oregon State University's College of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Sciences. He helped design, build and run NSF's Ocean Observatories Initiative, setting requirements and evaluating instruments and platforms, and since 2015 has managed operations of the OOI Endurance Array off the Pacific Northwest. Ph.D. from the MIT/WHOI Joint Program (1995).
updates.research_interests: cross-shelf exchange processes; analysis and prediction of Lagrangian transport; air-sea interaction; moored time series and surface drifter observations; OOI Northeast Pacific Endurance Array operations

updates.name: Elizabeth T. Keppeler
updates.bio: Hydrologist at the Pacific Southwest Research Station of the USDA Forest Service, listed among the staff of the Caspar Creek Experimental Watersheds. She co-authored the Forest Service data releases covering Caspar Creek Phase 1 (1962-1985) and Phase 2 (1985-2017) streamflow, sediment and climate records.
updates.research_interests: streamflow, sediment and hydrologic response to harvest and drought at the Caspar Creek Experimental Watersheds; groundwater and soil moisture in coast redwood forests; fog in managed redwood forests; hydroclimatic extremes and water quality in reference watersheds

updates.name: Ellen D. Ketterson
updates.bio: Distinguished Professor Emerita of Biology at Indiana University Bloomington. Her lab manipulates hormones in free-living dark-eyed juncos ('phenotypic engineering') to learn how selection shapes integrated life histories, tracing testosterone's effects on behavior, physiology and reproductive success, and has also examined what controls migration timing, distance and site fidelity.
updates.research_interests: phenotypic engineering; testosterone and life-history evolution; dark-eyed junco; extra-pair mating and parental behavior; avian migration timing and site fidelity

updates.name: Emile H. Elias
updates.bio: Hydrologist who has worked as a USDA Agricultural Research Service research hydrologist and director of the USDA Southwest Climate Hub. Her research covers how land use and climate change affect Southwestern water, water quality and farming communities, including snowmelt runoff and drought learning networks. She co-authored the Southwest chapter of the Fifth National Climate Assessment.
updates.research_interests: land-use and climate-change impacts on Southwest hydrology and water quality; climate impacts on snowmelt runoff in western streams; drought learning networks; decision-support tools for agriculture; landscape dynamics of vector-borne disease
